title: LLaVAShield: Safeguarding Multimodal Multi-Turn Dialogues in Vision-Language Models
measurement_description: The paper measures the safety moderation capabilities and robustness of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in multimodal multi-turn dialogues. It evaluates the models' ability to detect unsafe content across an 8-dimension safety taxonomy, which includes 'Religious hate (attacks based on beliefs)' as a sub-dimension under the 'Hate & Harassment' category.
findings: The paper does not report isolated findings specific to religion or religious hate. Broadly, it finds that advanced VLMs and existing moderation tools struggle significantly to detect composite safety risks (including hate speech and harassment) in multimodal multi-turn dialogues, while the newly proposed LLaVAShield model successfully identifies these complex threats and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
